summary: Verified and corrected a residual UnifiedRadixCache empty-finished-request path relevant to Qwen4Exp hybrid Mamba serving. When no Mamba track boundary had been reached, cache_finished_req continued with an empty key and adopted the root as last_node despite holding no root lock. The fix mirrors the existing unfinished-request guard, releases request-owned KV/Mamba resources without inserting, and makes direct empty inserts explicit no-ops. This is a verified candidate for one accumulation mechanism, not a reproduction of the reported 24-hour acceptance decay.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before GPU regression: 2 failed and 2 passed. A finished request with no Mamba track boundary was repointed from its matched node to the root, and direct empty insertion returned the root as last_device_node. Raw output: reports/j-d193e55bef04/raw/regression-before.txt

Passing-after GPU regression: 4 passed, covering no-boundary cleanup and node ownership, a positive track-boundary insertion, zero-length request cleanup, and direct empty insertion. Raw output: reports/j-d193e55bef04/raw/regression-after.txt
GPU regression plus adjacent UnifiedRadixCache suite: 1214 passed, 1362 skipped, 58 subtests passed. Raw output: reports/j-d193e55bef04/raw/regression-and-adjacent-after.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: Tests executed with HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, ISA gfx950, using Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. The fixture allocated real KV and Mamba pools and checked GPU-backed cache behavior and allocator conservation.

remaining_limitations: The reported RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 weights were unavailable, and the source workload requires two SM121 DGX Spark nodes with TP=2; no full-model, SM121, multi-node, or 24-hour uptime reproduction was performed.

The test verifies transport-independent UnifiedRadixCache state ownership and resource conservation only. It does not establish semantic accuracy or prove that this is the only cause of NEXTN acceptance decay.

Issue comments report that the older legacy-cache ghost-node fix and both speculative tracking clamps did not prevent relapse in one deployment, so those changes alone are not claimed as a solution here.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
